assemblage_scale.interpretation: The assemblage-level island phenotype is dominated by species composition rather than positive morphology information beyond species identity.

structural_morphology_persistence.interpretation: Island-associated structural morphology is detectable within years but does not transfer materially across years.

isotopic_niche_sensitivity.role: secondary sensitivity only because blood isotopes integrate pre-breeding foraging and are not local summer island-foraging measurements

supported: apparent functional differentiation among Palmer breeding sites is strongly compositional at the assemblage scale
within Adelie penguins, fixed island morphology effects are weak over the three-year Palmer Penguins window
structural morphology contains modest same-year island information but that information is nearly lost when transferred to a different year
repeated sign reversals of pairwise island contrasts are concordant with temporal reassembly rather than a stable island-specific phenotype
species sorting and year-specific within-species structure can jointly generate an apparent island phenotype without requiring a persistent local ecotype
not_supported: local adaptation to individual Palmer islands
a causal snow, habitat, competition, or foraging mechanism
a general island-biogeographic law from three islands and three years
a claim that isotope differences represent local summer island foraging
